This guide maps the public model workflow to the R and native subsystems that
implement it. The supported entry point is the `GEModel` reference-class
generator. Call its methods to load a TABLO model and data, configure a
closure and shocks, solve, and inspect results. For full-size, unaggregated
GTAP data, use the sparse runtime: the original in-memory path was not
practical for the complete workload. The legacy engine remains the default
for API compatibility and is useful for smaller models. Compiler, index,
cache, and source-data fields are implementation state; they are not supported
mutation inputs.

```r
model = GEModelR::GEModel$new()
model$loadTablo("model.tab")
model$loadData(input_data, engine = "sparse")
model$setClosure("tax")
model$setShocks(setNames(4, 'tax["south"]'))
model$solveModel(engine = "sparse", backend = "Matrix")
```

## From TABLO text to a model runtime

`loadTablo()` runs the TABLO parser and prepares both the legacy generators
and the sparse specification. For sparse execution, the compiler turns
supported equation and update forms into indexed structures used by the
sparse runtime, avoiding the complete dense in-memory system. The legacy path
creates R functions for data skeletons, coefficients, variables, and updates
and remains available for smaller workloads and compatibility. Select the
runtime with `loadData(engine = "legacy" or "sparse")`; `solveModel()` must
use that same engine. The engine is the model runtime choice, while `backend`
selects an implementation within the sparse runtime.

| Responsibility | Main source files |
|---|---|
| Public orchestration and runtime dispatch | `R/GEModel.R` |
| Sparse equation and update compilation | `R/sparseCompiler.R` |
| Sparse indexing, emission, solve acceptance, and diagnostics | `R/sparseSolver.R`, `R/sparsePartition.R`, `R/sparseElimination.R`, `R/sparseSchur*.R` |
| Native sparse LU, Schur, and block-elimination kernels | `src/sparse-lu.cpp`, `src/sparse-schur*.cpp`, `src/sparse-elimination.cpp` |
| Optional native capability checks and R adapters | `R/zzzSparseSchurCpp.R`, `R/zzzzSparseSchurOpenMP.R` |
| Legacy TABLO statements and generators | `R/tabloToStatements.R`, `R/processTablo.R`, `R/*Statement.R`, `R/*Generator.R` |

## Solver and native boundaries

The sparse `Matrix` backend is the supported general-purpose default. The
supported `StructuredSchur` and `StructuredSchurFGMRES` R backends use a
validated partition when the model has the required structure. `SparseM` and
`StructuredSchurFGMRESCpp` are compatibility-only backend requests; they are
not supported solver choices. `SuiteSparse` is recognized but unavailable in
supported installed builds. A request that cannot run fails capability checks;
GEModelR does not silently substitute another backend. See the
[backend selection guide](backend-selection.html) for the current public
backend tiers.

Rcpp entry points are declared in the C++ sources and registered through the
generated `R/RcppExports.R` and `src/RcppExports.cpp` files. Regenerate these
wrappers with `Rcpp::compileAttributes()`; do not edit generated wrappers by
hand. Native code checks dimensions, storage, and finite values before use.
OpenMP workers operate on prepared native buffers; R API calls and R memory
allocation stay on the main thread. Serial builds remain supported.

The C++ optimization work targets sparse kernels such as triangular solves,
Schur accumulation, and block elimination. Sparse triangular solves share one
native kernel between serial and OpenMP execution. The kernel packs at most 32
right-hand sides into contiguous rows, then restores the caller's matrix
layout and permutations. Its temporary workspace is bounded by that tile
width. Worker buffers are allocated before entering OpenMP, and worker
failures are reported on the R thread. CSC storage and one-based positions are
validated before native indexing; dense factor handles are tagged and
released only by their owning implementation.

The C++ FGMRES A/B harness is development and qualification material. Its
candidate identifier is compatibility-only in the public API, so it is not a
production recommendation and its measurements do not guarantee a full-model
speedup. The [external benchmark guide](external-full-scale-benchmarking.html)
describes the harness and its input requirements.

## Numerical acceptance, diagnostics, and cleanup

A sparse backend returns a candidate solution. Before that candidate is
applied to model state, GEModelR checks its structure and finiteness and
recomputes the true residual against the emitted full sparse system. A
non-finite value, incompatible structure, or residual outside the configured
tolerance rejects the candidate without applying it. This acceptance gate is
shared across sparse backends; solver-specific diagnostics remain additional
evidence rather than a replacement for the true-residual check.

Every solve attempt replaces `model$lastDiagnostics` with a versioned outcome
envelope. Setting `diagnostics = TRUE` adds residual history, timings,
allocation and capability evidence, detailed cleanup status, and memory
estimates. Solve-scoped backend cleanup is recorded on success and failure.
Native dense factors have explicit release paths and finalizers. A
post-simulation failure is reported separately from numerical acceptance and
can be retried with `retryPostsim()` without another solve when the accepted
state is retained.

## Validation ownership

Small, deterministic parser and solver contracts belong in
`tests/testthat/`, with shared fixtures in `tests/testthat/fixtures/` and
helpers in `tests/testthat/helper-*.R`. The native CI workflow checks
installed solver contracts in serial builds on Linux, macOS, and Windows,
and OpenMP builds on Linux and Windows. The separate `benchmarks/` harnesses
own larger performance and full-scale comparisons; those runs use external
inputs and do not belong in ordinary package checks or documentation builds.
